Article.ArticleTitle: A pragmatic resistance band intervention to improve physical function in community-dwelling older adults: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Resistance training can slow sarcopenic decline and is a foundational lifestyle habit for maintaining health span and independence, yet participation remains low. We examined the effectiveness of an 18-week faded-contact resistance-band training program on physical function in community-dwelling preclinically mobility-limited older adults.

A randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted in older adults with self-reported preclinical mobility limitation (≥70 years), comparing a resistance band training (RBT) group with a non-exercise control (CON) group. The RBT group participated in a twice-weekly, 18-week, faded-contact, group-based full-body resistance band program. The primary outcome was physical function. Secondary outcomes included strength, power, body composition, sarcopenia risk, frailty status, mobility, habitual physical activity, and health-related quality of life, assessed at Week 0, 6, 12, and 18.

Sixty participants were randomized, and 59 (mean age 75 ± 4 years; 66% women) were analyzed (RBT n = 30; CON n = 29). Adherence to RBT was 91%. RBT improved function from week 0-12 in the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) (0.88 [95% CI: 0.29, 1.47]; p = 0.001) and tandem stand (0.62 [95% CI: 0.17, 1.07]; p = 0.003). The RBT group significantly improved in the 5 times sit-to-stand compared to CON from week 0-6 (-2.01 [95% CI: -3.34, -0.67]; p = 0.001), week 12 (-2.61 [95% CI: -3.95, -1.27]; p < 0.001), and week 18 (-1.85 [95% CI: -3.19, -0.50]; p = 0.003). At 18 weeks, D3-Creatine-measured muscle mass increased more in RBT than CON (1.07 kg [95% CI: 0.49, 1.65]; p < 0.001). RBT also improved relative sit-to-stand power compared to CON at weeks 6, 12, and 18, with the largest difference at week 12 (0.55 W/kg [95% CI: 0.28, 0.83]; p < 0.001). No interactions were observed for other secondary outcomes. Clinically relevant SPPB change occurred only in RBT.

A pragmatic resistance-band training program delivered by exercise and health professionals to preclinically mobility-limited older adults increased physical function and D3-Creatine-measured muscle mass. These data provide insight into the effectiveness of resistance band training for maintaining and improving function and muscle mass.
